hints: Look at which side of the diagram is the anatomical right and left of the heart, and notice whether labels B and C point to upper thin-walled chambers or lower thick-walled chambers.
Remember the aorta forms the tall central arch with three small branches on top, while the pulmonary artery leaves the front of the heart toward the lungs, and atria sit above ventricles.
walkthrough:
**Orient yourself to the heart**

Think of this as looking at the front of a person facing you. So the left side of the diagram is the heart's right side, and the right side of the diagram is the heart's left side.

Atria are the smaller upper receiving chambers, ventricles are the larger lower pumping chambers with thicker muscle.

**Identify the big vessels at the top**

The large arch in the centre with three small branches on top is the aorta. Label A points to one of those upper branches, so it is part of the aorta, not the pulmonary artery.

Label D points to the vessel coming out in front and dividing toward the lungs. That is the pulmonary artery, not the aorta.

**Check the chambers B and C**

Label C points to the upper chamber on the left of the diagram. That is the anatomical right side, so it is the right atrium receiving deoxygenated blood from the vena cava. This matches.

Label B points to the upper chamber on the right of the diagram. That is the anatomical left side, so it is the left atrium, not the thick-walled left ventricle below it.

options.A: Label A points to a branch of the aortic arch at the very top, not the pulmonary artery which leaves lower down toward the lungs.
options.B: Label B points to the upper chamber on the heart's left side, which is the left atrium, not the thick-walled left ventricle below it.
options.C: Label C points to the upper chamber on the heart's right side, which is correctly the right atrium.
options.D: Label D points to the pulmonary trunk and artery in the middle front, not the large central aortic arch.
